findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 identifies current board as "WeirdML v3" and lists "WeirdML v2" only under "Previous versions: WeirdML v2 · WeirdML v1". Row declares version 2 and version_guard "Verify the published version 2 before reading results." This continuity is contradicted by the protocol, which now publishes v3.
findings.repair: Align version/version_guard and identity with WeirdML v3, or represent v2 explicitly as a retained/previous board with appropriate lifecycle fields.

findings.evidence: Row metric: "Average Max Accuracy: per task, mean over runs of the maximum test accuracy across the 5 iterations per run, averaged over all 17 tasks." SOURCE 1 defines the official score as "80% normalized area under its line... plus 20% of its final value" across 11 tasks and 15 configurations, and says effective scores "are not raw accuracy". No mention of 5 iterations or 17 tasks. SOURCE 3 only supports the percent/[0,100] scale, not the metric definition.
findings.repair: Replace scoring.metric with the protocol's official score definition (normalized area under best-so-far effective score over 500k–50M tokens, 11 tasks) or provide evidence for the claimed max-accuracy formula.

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 shows v3 is the maintained current board and v2 is a previous version. The row sets status="active", version_status="published", and superseded_by=null, but the protocol indicates v2 is replaced/retired and names successor WeirdML v3. Source 2's activity summary concerns today's payload for the current board (WeirdML v3/v3-era data), not v2, so it cannot establish v2 as active.
findings.repair: Set status="retained", version_status="retained", and set superseded_by to the successor board's registry id (likely the WeirdML v3 entry); do not claim current publication.

uncertainties: Owner-executed SHA-256, transport and qualification checks were not independently reproduced; this is a read-only limitation, not missing numeric source evidence.
The exact successor registry id for WeirdML v3 is not included in the packet, so the repair cannot state the precise superseded_by value; this does not change the mismatch finding.
The source-2 activity and source-3 value-scale summaries are this run's generated reads; they were used only for the status and unit/range checks as permitted, not to validate metric meaning.
